facts.statement: Dibothrosuchus is a genus of sphenosuchian, which is a type of basal crocodylomorph related to modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: Dibothrosuchus is a genus of sphenosuchian, a type of basal crocodylomorph, the clade that comprises the crocodilians and their closest kin.

facts.statement: The genus Dibothrosuchus was named in 1965 by D.J. Simmons based on fossils collected by Father Oehler near Huangchiatien.
facts.quote: Dibothrosuchus was named in 1965 by D.J. Simmons based on a partial skull and skeleton collected by Father Oehler of Fu Jen Catholic University from mudstones near Huangchiatien.

facts.statement: Additional remains of Dibothrosuchus were recovered in 1985 by a joint Chinese-US expedition.
facts.quote: Additional remains of this genus were recovered in 1985 by a joint Chinese-US expedition.

facts.statement: A second species, D. xingsuensis, was named by Wu in 1986 but is now considered a synonym of D. elaphros.
facts.quote: A second species, D. xingsuensis, was named by Wu in 1986.

facts.statement: Fossils of Dibothrosuchus were found in Lower Jurassic rocks approximately 186 million years old in Yunnan, China.
facts.quote: These fossils were found in Lower Jurassic (Lower Pliensbachian, circa 186 million years old) rocks of Yunnan, China.

facts.statement: Dibothrosuchus lived between 201.4 and 192.9 million years ago during the Hettangian to Sinemurian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Sinemurian (201.4 to 192.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Dibothrosuchus was a small animal with a skull 164 mm long and an estimated body length of 1.3 meters.
facts.quote: Dibothrosuchus was not a large animal. From the tip of the snout to the occipital condyle, the skull of IVPP V 7907 is only 164 mm long, and the body length of the individual is estimated as 1.3 m.

facts.statement: Dibothrosuchus had a slender body, long tail, long limbs, and a pointed snout.
facts.quote: In general form, Dibothrosuchus was a slender, long-tailed and long-limbed quadruped with a pointed snout.

facts.statement: Unlike modern crocodilians, Dibothrosuchus was a terrestrial animal.
facts.quote: Unlike modern crocodilians, it was a terrestrial animal.

facts.statement: The upper jaws of Dibothrosuchus had five teeth per premaxilla and seventeen per maxilla, with a hole allowing an enlarged lower jaw tooth to fit through.
facts.quote: The upper jaws had five small teeth per premaxilla (snout-tip bones) and seventeen per maxilla, with a small hole between the maxilla and premaxilla for an enlarged tooth in the lower jaw to fit.

facts.statement: Dibothrosuchus was originally classified as an ornithosuchid thecodont but was later reclassified as a sphenosuchian.
facts.quote: Dibothrosuchus was first described as an ornithosuchid thecodont, but it was later reclassified as a sphenosuchid sphenosuchian.

facts.statement: Dibothrosuchus belongs to the parent group Crocodylomorpha.
